title: ABB Frontend Development Bootcamp — Core Curriculum
description: The canonical six-month, 24-week track supplied for the ABB Frontend Development Bootcamp. Supplementary topics are listed separately and are not presented as original bootcamp weeks.

months.title: Web Fundamentals & Layout
months.goal: Write semantic HTML, use the CSS box model and layout systems, create responsive pages, and debug in browser DevTools.

weeks.title: Web and HTML Basics
topics: Internet, browser, HTTP, URL, request and response
Semantic elements: header, nav, main, section, article, footer
practice: Build a simple About Me page
Inspect elements and the DOM with DevTools

weeks.title: HTML Forms and Accessibility Basics
topics: form, input, select, textarea and button
label, placeholder, name, value and required
practice: Build login and registration form layouts
Connect labels to controls and test keyboard access

weeks.title: CSS Fundamentals
topics: Box model, margin, padding, border and box-sizing
practice: Build a small landing page with header, content and footer

weeks.title: Flexbox, Grid and Responsive Design
topics: Flexbox axes, justify-content, align-items and gap
Grid rows, columns, fr and repeat
practice: Build a responsive landing page for desktop and mobile

months.title: JavaScript Core & Git
months.goal: Understand JavaScript fundamentals, manipulate the DOM, handle asynchronous work, and use Git for a basic delivery workflow.

weeks.title: JavaScript Basics
practice: Solve 5–10 small tasks covering arrays, conditions and loops

weeks.title: Functions, Arrays and Objects
topics: Function declarations, expressions and arrow functions
map, filter, reduce, find, some and every
practice: Solve dataset exercises with array methods and object transformations

weeks.title: DOM and Events
practice: Build a To-do app using an in-memory array and DOM rendering

weeks.title: Async JavaScript and Git
topics: git init, add, commit, push and .gitignore
practice: Build a page that fetches public API data
Publish the project in a personal Git repository
weeks.project: Month 2 project: API-driven mini app with Git history

months.title: Tooling, TypeScript & Intro to React
months.goal: Set up JavaScript projects, model data with TypeScript, and build React interfaces using components, props and state.

weeks.title: Node, Package Managers and Project Setup
topics: Vite or Create React App project setup
practice: Create a React project and configure linting and formatting

weeks.title: TypeScript Basics
topics: string, number, boolean, any and unknown
A simple generic such as Array<T>
practice: Build a typed user-list module

weeks.title: React Fundamentals
practice: Build Counter and To-do components by rewriting previous tasks in React

weeks.title: React Hooks and Component Composition
practice: Build an API-powered News/Posts list with loading and error states

months.title: React Ecosystem: Routing, Forms, State and APIs
months.goal: Build a small SPA, validate forms, share state across components, and separate API access from UI components.

weeks.title: Routing
topics: React Router: Routes, Link and useParams
practice: Build a 2–3 page SPA with Home, About and Posts routes

weeks.title: Forms and Validation
practice: Build a registration/login form with validation messages

weeks.title: State Management Patterns
topics: Reducing prop drilling and simple global state
practice: Build a theme toggle and a global user-state example

weeks.title: API Integration and Custom Hooks
topics: Custom hooks such as useUsers and usePosts
Error handling and an introduction to retry strategies
practice: Build a dashboard with multiple API calls, filters and search

months.title: UI Systems, Performance, Accessibility, Testing and Workflow
months.goal: Design reusable UI pieces, improve performance and accessibility, write component tests, and understand team delivery workflows.

weeks.title: UI Kit and Design System Thinking
topics: UI libraries such as Chakra UI or MUI
practice: Build a small UI kit with Button, Input and Card components

weeks.title: Performance and Accessibility
topics: React.memo, useMemo and useCallback at an introductory level
practice: Tune an existing project and inspect bundle size or lazy routes

weeks.title: Testing with Jest Concepts and React Testing Library
topics: Why test, unit vs integration testing
practice: Write 2–3 component tests for interactions such as button click and form submission

weeks.title: Git Workflow and CI/CD Basics
topics: Build and test stages in a CI/CD pipeline
practice: Simulate task → branch → commit → MR → review

months.title: Capstone Project and Professional Skills
months.goal: Plan, implement, review, test, refine and present a complete frontend application.

weeks.title: Capstone Requirements and Design — Part 1
practice: Define the problem, target users, core stories and acceptance criteria

weeks.title: Capstone Requirements and Design — Part 2
practice: Produce wireframes, an API contract sketch, a page map and sprint plan

weeks.title: Capstone Implementation
topics: API integration, routing, forms and global state
CRUD, basic authentication when required and critical tests
practice: Implement the project's core end-to-end user journeys

weeks.title: Refactoring, Testing and Demo
practice: Present the final application and explain architecture, trade-offs and code quality
weeks.project: Final Capstone Project and Demo Day

supplementaryTracks.title: JavaScript Runtime and Language Internals
supplementaryTracks.note: Supplementary depth beyond the weekly bootcamp outline; align with the user's Notion notes.

supplementaryTracks.title: Frontend Architecture and Engineering Depth
supplementaryTracks.note: Extend the curriculum with practical, production-oriented architecture decisions.

supplementaryTracks.title: Authentication and Authorization
topics: Secure storage and common browser threats
supplementaryTracks.note: Supplementary security track; examples require current primary-source verification.

supplementaryTracks.title: Build, Deployment and Hosting
supplementaryTracks.note: Expands the final weeks with operational understanding.

supplementaryTracks.title: SQL, PostgreSQL and Supabase
supplementaryTracks.note: Supplementary track; not represented as part of the original 24-week core syllabus.

supplementaryTracks.title: Development Tooling and Package Management
supplementaryTracks.note: Expands Week 9 tooling into a deeper reference track.
